title: High DRS Migration Activity
exclusions: Counts documented DRS-recommended migration events; it does not measure cluster imbalance, failed recommendations, migration duration, application impact, or causality. Twenty per hour is local policy, not a VMware limit. Manual migrations are excluded. Missing cluster arguments/events and stale collection are source-health failures. The UC does not change DRS automation or placement.
evidence: Retain `vmware_high_drs_migration_activity`, raw events/keys, collection health, cluster inventory/size and DRS mode/rules, approved threshold/baseline, rows and dispositions, matching vSphere Tasks and Events, and dated 20/21 boundary, duplicate, multi-VM, blank-cluster, manual-migration, maintenance and late-data tests. Editorial review created no DRS action or production evidence.

controlTest.positiveScenario: Index 21 distinct DrsVmMigratedEvent fixtures for cluster `prod-cluster-1` inside the closed hour, spanning seven VM names and unique keys. Expect one row with drs_migrations=21, distinct_vms=7 and threshold_migrations=20; replay one key and the count remains 21.
controlTest.negativeScenario: Expect zero rows for exactly 20 DRS migrations, any number of plain VmMigratedEvent records, blank cluster identity, blank key, wrong source/index, or events outside the hour. Source-health must separately expose absent cluster extraction or delayed event collection.

dataSources: Splunk Add-on for VMware (Splunkbase 3215) vCenter API `event` task into documented default `index=vmware-taskevent`, `sourcetype=vmware:events`. Required evidence: DrsVmMigratedEvent token, key, computeResource.name or validated cluster alias, `_time`; vm.name and collector host support distinct-VM and replay analysis. DRS configuration/recommendations and host CPU/memory are corroboration.
app: Splunk Add-on for VMware (`Splunk_TA_vmware` and `SA-Hydra`, Splunkbase 3215) for vCenter API collection; Splunk Add-on for VMware Indexes (Splunkbase 5640) and Splunk Add-on for VMware Extractions (Splunkbase 5641) are deployment components required by current packaging. A local virtualization-operations app owns searches, lookups, dashboards, scripted inputs where stated, and runbooks.
spl:
index=vmware-taskevent sourcetype="vmware:events" "DrsVmMigratedEvent" earliest=-75m@m latest=-15m@m
| spath path=key output=event_key
| spath path=computeResource.name output=cluster_name
| spath path=vm.name output=vm_name
| eval event_key=coalesce(event_key,key), cluster_name=coalesce(cluster_name,cluster,'computeResource.name'), vm_name=coalesce(vm_name,'vm.name')
| where len(tostring(event_key))>0 AND len(cluster_name)>0
| eval event_identity=host."|".event_key
| dedup event_identity
| stats count as drs_migrations dc(vm_name) as distinct_vms values(vm_name) as vm_names values(event_key) as event_keys min(_time) as first_event max(_time) as last_event by cluster_name
| where drs_migrations>20
| eval use_case_id="UC-2.1.8", threshold_migrations=20, window="60 minutes", local_severity="medium"
| table cluster_name drs_migrations distinct_vms vm_names event_keys first_event last_event threshold_migrations window local_severity use_case_id
| sort 0 -drs_migrations cluster_name
description: Reports a vSphere cluster when more than 20 deduplicated DrsVmMigratedEvent records occur in a delayed closed hour, retaining distinct VM count, event identities, and observation bounds.
value: Unusually frequent DRS-directed movement can expose unstable demand, constrained placement choices, affinity conflicts, maintenance activity, or an unsuitable local policy. A transparent count gives platform owners a focused cluster review without falsely labeling movement as imbalance.
implementation: Enable event collection and validate DrsVmMigratedEvent plus computeResource/VM arguments. Run hourly over a delayed closed hour. Treat more than 20 as a local starting policy, baseline separately by cluster size and automation mode, and do not call the finding DRS instability without recommendation, demand, rule, host-state, and workload evidence.
visualization: Dashboard `vSphere DRS Activity`: event-source and cluster-field health first; hourly migration count with per-cluster policy line; distinct VM count; top moved VMs; cluster table with DRS mode, host count, CPU/memory headroom, active maintenance, affinity-rule state, owner and exception. Default 24 hours, 30-day baseline; drill to raw events and vSphere Cluster > Monitor > vSphere DRS > Recommendations/History.

references.title: Splunk Add-on for VMware source types

knownFalsePositives:
1. **Approved host maintenance evacuation** — DRS may move many VMs from a host entering maintenance. Verify task/change, source host, affected VM set and successful completion; use a finite cluster/time exception in `vmware_uc_dispositions.csv` only for notification.

2. **Cluster expansion or contraction** — adding or removing a host can drive legitimate placement changes. Compare inventory and change record, then ensure activity decays and constraints remain satisfied.

3. **Planned load or resilience test** — a benchmark or failover rehearsal can cause real DRS movement. Verify named test, workload set, owner, expected count window and post-test stability; never wildcard the cluster permanently.

4. **Event replay or overlapping collectors** — duplicate keys can inflate activity after checkpoint recovery or duplicate DCNs. Compare collector plus event key and indexing delay; the search deduplicates its window, while source owners fix persistent duplication.

Delivery suppression uses the governed lookup table `vmware_uc_dispositions.csv` only after the base result is retained; each entry requires the exact UC/entity keys, owner, ticket, reason, start, and finite expiry.
reviewer: Source-backed editorial review; production VMware/Splunk SME validation pending
detailedImplementation:
## Prerequisites and source contract

This is a documentation-reviewed implementation, not a record that the search ran in production. Use Splunk Add-on for VMware (Splunkbase 3215) with its compatible `Splunk_TA_vmware` and `SA-Hydra` packages. Current packaging also requires the VMware Indexes and Extractions packages on the tiers named by Splunk's installation guide. The scheduler assigns API jobs to Data Collection Nodes; a DCN must reach vCenter over HTTPS and forward collected data to the indexer. Use a dedicated vCenter account whose effective privileges have been tested against the inventory, performance, task, or event objects required here. Do not copy an unverified role name from this page.

The indexes in the SPL are Splunk's documented defaults from `ta_vmware_collection.conf`: `index=vmware-perf`, `index=vmware-inv`, and `index=vmware-taskevent`. If local index names differ, change only the base index after proving equivalent routing and access. The relevant documented default tasks are `hostvmperf`, `otherperf`, `datastoreinv`, `vminv`, and `event`; enable only the task named below. Keep vCenter, scheduler, DCNs, indexers, and search heads time-synchronized. Install matching search-time extractions before relying on extracted fields.

## Step 1 — Configure and verify collection

Enable `event` at the documented 300-second default. VMware defines DrsVmMigratedEvent narrowly: a VM migration recommended by DRS. Validate the serialized computeResource cluster argument and event key in raw data. Maintain governed cluster inventory with DRS automation mode, host count, maintenance state and affinity/anti-affinity rules; the event stream alone cannot diagnose imbalance.

Before saving the analytic, run a discovery search over at least two expected collection intervals:

```spl
index=vmware-taskevent sourcetype="vmware:events" earliest=-2h "DrsVmMigratedEvent"
| stats count latest(_time) as latest_event dc(key) as distinct_keys by host
| convert ctime(latest_event)
```

Confirm the expected entities appear, compare them with the named vSphere or PowerCLI view, and inspect representative `_raw` events. Verify every required field rather than treating a sourcetype count as proof of semantic completeness. Record the add-on version, collection task, configured interval, target index, vCenter, entity scope, and p95/p99 indexing delay. A missing entity or stale poll is a source-health finding and must not be interpreted as a healthy virtualization condition.

## Step 2 — Create and understand the search

Save the sidecar SPL verbatim as `vmware_high_drs_migration_activity` after substituting only an approved local index name. Run hourly using `earliest=-75m@m latest=-15m@m`. Move both bounds together after measuring p99 delay so buckets remain nonoverlapping.

```spl
index=vmware-taskevent sourcetype="vmware:events" "DrsVmMigratedEvent" earliest=-75m@m latest=-15m@m
| spath path=key output=event_key
| spath path=computeResource.name output=cluster_name
| spath path=vm.name output=vm_name
| eval event_key=coalesce(event_key,key), cluster_name=coalesce(cluster_name,cluster,'computeResource.name'), vm_name=coalesce(vm_name,'vm.name')
| where len(tostring(event_key))>0 AND len(cluster_name)>0
| eval event_identity=host."|".event_key
| dedup event_identity
| stats count as drs_migrations dc(vm_name) as distinct_vms values(vm_name) as vm_names values(event_key) as event_keys min(_time) as first_event max(_time) as last_event by cluster_name
| where drs_migrations>20
| eval use_case_id="UC-2.1.8", threshold_migrations=20, window="60 minutes", local_severity="medium"
| table cluster_name drs_migrations distinct_vms vm_names event_keys first_event last_event threshold_migrations window local_severity use_case_id
| sort 0 -drs_migrations cluster_name
```

Understanding this SPL: The class token restricts the source to DRS-recommended migrations. Event key dedup prevents replay inflation; `stats` creates one cluster row for the hour and retains VM/event evidence. A strict `>20` local rule means 21 is the first qualifying count. No statistical or causal claim is hidden.

The query emits stable columns and preserves the observed values needed for triage. Its threshold or status filter is an explicit local monitoring policy, not a VMware universal limit unless the cited VMware source says otherwise. Keep the unsuppressed result as evidence. Apply delivery suppression only after the row exists through a governed `vmware_uc_dispositions.csv` lookup keyed by `use_case_id` plus the exact entity key, with owner, ticket, reason, start time, and finite `exception_until`; expired, malformed, or wildcard entries must not suppress.

## Step 3 — Validate semantics and controls

Compare one busy and one quiet cluster with vSphere Client **Cluster > Monitor > vSphere DRS > History** and Tasks and Events for the same closed hour. Confirm event keys, cluster argument and distinct VM count. Validate 20/21 boundary with fixtures; use historical approved maintenance for volume comparison rather than inducing production moves.

Run the positive and negative `controlTest` scenarios in an isolated search index or lab vCenter. Assert the exact row count and output fields. Also test duplicate input, null required fields, wrong sourcetype/index, events outside the scheduled window, late indexing, and reruns. Compare raw values with the authoritative vSphere Client or PowerCLI result identified above. Measure source coverage, latest event age, duplicate rate, field-null rate, scheduler skips, search runtime, and alert delivery. Keep `status=draft` until VMware, Splunk, service ownership, and operations reviewers approve the data contract and runtime results.

## Step 4 — Operationalize and investigate

Validate events/count; determine maintenance or topology change; inspect DRS mode/recommendations and moved VM repetition; compare host/cluster CPU and memory demand, reservations, limits, admission headroom and affinity rules; correlate storage/network constraints and workload schedules; classify planned movement, demand shift, constraint conflict, collector replay or unresolved condition; tune only from documented baselines.

Use the dashboard design in `visualization`. Put source health before findings so silence cannot render as green. Restrict raw event, user, VM, datastore, and infrastructure identifiers to roles with an operational need. Alert titles must describe the observed metric, state, or event; they must not claim root cause, outage, data loss, unauthorized activity, or successful remediation without corroboration.

## Step 5 — Troubleshoot safely

If all events lack cluster, inspect raw computeResource argument and extraction package; do not group by collector host as a substitute. If counts differ from vSphere, align event time, delay and class. If one VM dominates, inspect its constraints and repeated source/destination sequence. If `DrsVmMigratedEvent` is absent while migrations occur, verify DRS origin versus manual migration and event collection scope.

For no data, verify the exact collection task in the scheduler, DCN assignment and health, vCenter credential reach, API scope, target index, extraction package, and time synchronization. Splunk documents that inventory JSON can exceed the default `spath` extraction cutoff; inspect `_raw` and adjust the supported search-command limit only when truncation is demonstrated. For stale or partial inventory, remember that the add-on performs full inventory followed by change sets and later full refreshes. For missing VM performance, verify hierarchy collection and the generated VM managed-object list. Do not change vSphere resources merely to make a monitor pass.

Closure requires a healthy source contract, a reconciled authoritative view, a documented owner decision, and an observed recovery or accepted finite exception. This UC performs no automatic vMotion, restart, snapshot removal, datastore expansion, alarm reset, host remediation, or vSAN repair.
grandmaExplanation: We point out when the automatic scheduler moves an unusually large number of machines in an hour, so the team can check whether it was planned or a sign of unstable conditions.
